source_text: Quonram autem quidam ex his qui putantur recte credidisse, supergrediuntur ordinem promotionis justorum, et modos meditationis ad incorruptelam ignorant, hzereticos sensus in se habentes: heeretici enim despicientes plasmationem Dei, et non suscipientes salutem carnis suze, contemnentes autem et repromissionem Dei, et totum supergredientes Deum sensu, simul atque mortui fuerint, dicunt se supergredi ccelos et Demiurgum, et ire ad matrem, vel ad eum qui ab ipsis affingitur, patrem. Qui ergo universam reprobant resurrectionem, et quantum in ipsis est auferunt eam de medio, quid mirum est, si nec ordinem resurrectionis sciunt, nointelligere, quoniam si heec ita essent, quemadmodum dicunt, ipse utique Dominus, in quem se dicunt credere, non in tertia die fecisset resurrectionem; sed super crucem exspirans, confestim utique abiisset sursum, relinquens corpus terre? Nunc autem tribus diebus conversatus est ubi erant mortui, quemadpropheta ait de eo: Commemoratus est Dominus sanctorum mortuorum suorum, eorum qui ante dormierunt in terra sepelitionis, et descendit ad eos, extrahere eos, et salvare eos. Nemo enim est discipulus super magistrum : perfectus autem omnis, erit | sicut magister ejus. Quomodo ergo magister noster non statim evolans abiit, sed sustinens definitum a Patre resurrectionis suze tempus, quod et per Jonam manifestatum est, post triduum resurgens assumtus est; sic et nos sustinere debemus definitum a Deo resurrectionis nostree tempus, preenuntiatum a prophetis, et sic resurgentes assumi, quotquot Dominus ad hoc dignos habuerit*,
pass_a_gloss: For certain of those who are thought to have believed rightly, nevertheless overstep the order of the promotion of the just, and the modes of meditation to incorruptibility, having heretical senses in themselves: for heretics, despising the creation of God, and not receiving the salvation of their own flesh, but also despising the promise of God, and overstepping God in sense, as soon as they have died, say that they overstep the heavens and the Demiurge, and go to the mother, or to him who is affixed by them, the father. Who therefore reject the whole resurrection, and as far as it is in them, take it away from the midst, what wonder is it, if they do not know the order of the resurrection, nor understand, since if these things were as they say, the Lord himself, in whom they say they believe, would not have made the resurrection on the third day; but having expired on the cross, would have gone up immediately, leaving the body to the earth? But now, having conversed for three days where the dead were, as the prophet says of him: The Lord is mindful of his holy ones, who slept before on the earth of burial, and he descended to them, to draw them out and save them. And the Lord himself says: As Jonas was in the belly of the whale for three days and three nights, so will the Son of Man be in the earth. But also the Apostle says: He ascended, what is it, if not that he also descended into the lower parts of the earth? And David, prophesying about him, said: You have rescued my soul from the lowest hell. But rising again on the third day, and Mary, who first saw him, adored, saying: Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to the Father, but go to the disciples and say to them: I ascend to my Father and your Father. If therefore the Lord observed the law of the dead, so that he might become the firstborn from the dead, and having stayed until the third day among the dead of the earth, then rising again in the flesh, so that he might also show the marks of the nails to the disciples, thus he ascended to the Father, how are those not confounded, who say that the lower world is indeed this world, which is according to us; but the inner man of theirs, leaving the body here, ascends to a supercelestial place? For when the Lord went away in the midst of the shadow of death, where the souls of the dead were, then afterwards he rose again bodily, and after the resurrection he was taken up: it is manifest that also the souls of his disciples, for whom the Lord also worked these things, will go to an invisible place, defined for them by God, and there they will stay until the resurrection, sustaining the resurrection: afterwards receiving bodies, and rising again perfectly, that is, bodily, just as the Lord rose again, thus they will come to the sight of God. For no one is a disciple above the master: but every perfect one will be as his master. How therefore our master did not immediately fly away, but sustaining the defined time of his resurrection by the Father, which was also manifested through Jonas, rising again after three days, was taken up; so also we ought to sustain the defined time of our resurrection by God, preannounced by the prophets, and thus rising again, be taken up, as many as the Lord will have deemed worthy.

pass_b_english: Some who are thought to have believed rightly nevertheless overstep the order of the just's promotion and ignore the modes of meditation that lead to incorruptibility, because they harbor heretical notions. Heretics despise God's creation and refuse to accept the salvation of their own flesh; they also scorn God's promise and presume to overstep God in their thinking. As soon as they die, they claim they will overstep the heavens and the Demiurge and go to the Mother, or to the Father whom they have fabricated. Since they reject the resurrection entirely and, as far as they can, remove it from the picture, why should it surprise us that they do not know the order of the resurrection or understand it? For if things were as they say, the Lord himself, in whom they claim to believe, would not have risen on the third day; instead, expiring on the cross, he would have gone up at once, leaving his body to the earth.

But he spent three days among the dead, just as the prophet says of him: "The Lord is mindful of his holy ones, who slept before on the earth of burial, and he descended to them, to draw them out and save them" (cf. Ps 16:10). The Lord himself said: "As Jonah was in the belly of the whale three days and three nights, so will the Son of Man be in the heart of the earth" (Jonah 1:17). The Apostle also says: "He ascended -- what does this mean except that he also descended into the lower parts of the earth?" (Ephesians 4:9). And David, prophesying about him, said: "You have rescued my soul from the lowest hell" (Ps 16:10). Rising on the third day, he appeared to Mary, who saw him first; she worshiped him, but he said, "Do not hold on to me, for I have not yet ascended to the Father. Go instead to my brothers and tell them: I am ascending to my Father and your Father" (John 20:17).

If the Lord kept the law of the dead so that he might become the firstborn from the dead, staying until the third day among the dead of the earth, then rising bodily to show the disciples the nail marks, and only then ascending to the Father, how can those not be confounded who claim the lower world is this present world, while their inner self, leaving the body here, ascends to a supercelestial place? When the Lord went into the midst of death's shadow, where the souls of the dead were, he afterward rose bodily, and after the resurrection he was taken up. It is therefore clear that the souls of his disciples, for whose sake the Lord did all these things, will go to an invisible place appointed for them by God, and there they will remain until the resurrection, awaiting it. Then, receiving bodies and rising perfectly -- that is, bodily, just as the Lord rose -- they will come into God's sight. No disciple is above the master; the fully trained will be like the master. Since our Master did not fly away at once but waited for the resurrection time appointed by the Father, revealed through Jonah, and rose after three days before being taken up, we too must wait for the resurrection time appointed by God, announced by the prophets, and so, rising, be taken up -- as many as the Lord deems worthy.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful literal gloss, and Pass B provides a fluent translation that correctly identifies and expands the scripture citations (Psalm 16:10, Jonah 1:17, Ephesians 4:9, John 20:17) which were alluded to in the Latin. The distinction between the 'lower world' (inferos) and 'hell' is handled correctly in the lemmas and Pass B. All clauses, including the complex conditional arguments regarding the resurrection and the souls of the disciples, are preserved.
